newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga sees continuing fall in exploration costs.
newsitem.headline: Saga sees continuing fall in exploration costs.

text.p: Norwegian independent oil company Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it expected exploration costs on the Norwegian continental shelf to continue to fall.

In a presentation of the company's eight-month results, Saga said exploration costs had steadily declined since 1991, averaging 12.5 crowns per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) over the last five years and nine crowns over the last three years.
In 1991 the cost of discovering hydrocarbon reserves was 18 crowns per boe, the company said.
"We think the declining trend will continue in 1996," said Terje Hagevang, Saga's section head for exploration.
